extracted.intended_audience: policy analysts, advocacy organizations, regulated stakeholders submitting public comments on federal economic regulations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing public comments intended to influence economically significant federal rulemakings, emphasizing quantified analysis, engagement with agency regulatory impact analyses, and statutory/regulatory standards. Useful for organizations or stakeholders seeking to improve the technical quality and policy influence of their submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantified economic impact analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: AAF emphasizes the importance of quantified economic impact analysis in comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide quantitative impact estimates rather than qualitative assertions. Use verifiable data and clearly state assumptions; engage the agency's cost estimates and identification of missed costs/benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act burden estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Include estimates of paperwork burden under the Paperwork Reduction Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify hours and associated costs where the rule imposes information collection requirements; tie estimates to PRA procedures and OMB information collection review where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost–benefit framework engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage the agency's cost-benefit framework as part of comment analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss how the agency applied cost–benefit principles, note omissions or methodological issues, and reference OMB and agency guidance on cost–benefit analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cumulative regulatory cost considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider and analyze cumulative regulatory costs across rulemakings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the proposed rule's costs in the context of total regulatory burden and any trends in annual regulatory costs, rather than treating the rule in isolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small business impact (Regulatory Flexibility Act) analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Address impacts on small businesses consistent with the Regulatory Flexibility Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide analyses or estimates of effects on small entities, discuss whether a regulatory flexibility analysis is adequate, and suggest alternatives or exemptions where burdens are significant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federalism considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss federalism implications of the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify state/local impacts and potential conflicts with state authority; reference Executive Orders or statutes concerning federalism when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded mandate considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze whether the rule creates unfunded mandates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify or describe costs imposed on state, local, or tribal governments without federal funding; reference the Unfunded Mandates Reform Act where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite OMB Circular A-4 standards explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly cite OMB Circular A-4 standards in comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use A-4's recommended practices for economic analysis (e.g., identification of benefits and costs, discounting, treatment of uncertainty) as the benchmark when critiquing or supporting agency RIAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide cost estimates with verifiable assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide cost estimates that include verifiable assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State assumptions clearly, show calculations or models, and provide sources so agency reviewers can validate the estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with the agency's RIA methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage directly with the agency's Regulatory Impact Analysis (RIA) methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critically assess the agency's methods, data sources, and modeling choices; identify methodological weaknesses and suggest concrete improvements or alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address the agency's discount rate choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss and critique the agency's choice of discount rate in cost–benefit calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain implications of alternative discount rates, reference OMB guidance, and quantify sensitivity of results to the discount rate where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify benefits or costs the agency missed
rubrics_metrics.description: Point out benefits or costs the agency failed to include in its analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence or estimates for omitted effects and explain why inclusion would materially affect the agency's conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite Information Quality Act / Data Quality Act standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Information Quality Act (Data Quality Act) standards when challenging data or analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point to specific data quality issues in the agency's record, request corrections under applicable data-quality procedures, and cite the statutory/administrative standard used by OMB/agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address impacts on innovation and competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze how the rule might affect innovation and market competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence or theoretical reasoning on whether the rule will spur or hinder innovation, create barriers to entry, or affect competitive dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference specific OIRA-tracked metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference metrics tracked by OIRA when relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie comments to OIRA's tracked measures (e.g., quantified annual costs, paperwork burdens, major rule numbers) to situate the rule within broader executive-branch oversight metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific section citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite specific sections of the proposed rule or regulatory text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anchor critiques to particular provisions and regulatory text rather than making generalized statements; this improves the comment's usefulness to agency drafters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent data or analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Support comments with independent data or original analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide proprietary, academic, or other independent evidence to corroborate claims and strengthen credibility versus uncited assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggest alternatives with comparative analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer alternative regulatory approaches and analyze them comparatively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present feasible alternatives, quantify or qualitatively compare their costs and benefits to the agency's proposal, and explain tradeoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain-language clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Write comments in plain language for clarity and accessibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be concise and clear so agency staff can readily understand the argument and the supporting evidence; avoid unnecessary jargon while preserving technical accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pure expressions of preference
rubrics_metrics.description: AAF considers pure expressions of preference to be low-quality comment content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on statements like 'I oppose this rule' without providing substantive, evidence-backed analysis relevant to the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid generic concerns about overregulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic claims about 'overregulation' are considered low-quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on concrete regulatory effects and provisions rather than broad rhetoric about regulatory philosophy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid uncited claims about economic impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Uncited assertions about economic impacts are low-quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always support impact claims with data, citations, or transparent calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid ideological framing without substantive analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideological framing that lacks substantive technical analysis is low-quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If making normative or ideological points, couple them with empirical evidence or concrete legal/administrative arguments tied to the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tie comments to specific provisions (do not leave untied)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments not tied to specific provisions are viewed as low-quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the analysis or recommendation applies to particular regulatory paragraphs, sections, or rule language to make the comment actionable for agencies.
